code_signatures.detail: Inferno Drainer config flag. When true, the drainer exfiltrates a counterfactually-generated contract address to its backend to evade anti-phishing browser extensions.
code_signatures.source: Reverse engineering by Bernhard Mueller (Medium, 'A Peek Inside Inferno Drainer')

code_signatures.detail: Inferno backend handshake field. Page JS building a 'futurContract' value and POSTing wallet data to a /salt-style endpoint is Inferno's phishing-warning bypass.
code_signatures.source: Reverse engineering by Bernhard Mueller (Medium) — observed POST /salt payload {walletAddress, salt, futurContract, site}

code_signatures.detail: Permit selector appearing in frontend JS bundled with multicall logic matches Angel Drainer's documented drain sequence. Legit permit flows exist, so this is corroborating evidence, not a conviction on its own.
code_signatures.source: Check Point Research — Angel Drainer multicall executing Permit (0xd505accf) followed by transferFrom (0x23b872dd) against stETH

code_signatures.detail: The literal string 'drainer' in page JS. Rare in legitimate code; common in kit config and affiliate dashboards.
code_signatures.source: Heuristic — kit code, comments, and config frequently self-reference

0x095ea7b3.name: approve(address,uint256)
0x095ea7b3.risk: ERC-20 approval — unlimited amount = full token drain authorization

0x23b872dd.name: transferFrom(address,address,uint256)
0x23b872dd.risk: Moves tokens out of a victim wallet using a previously granted allowance

0x39509351.name: increaseAllowance(address,uint256)
0x39509351.risk: Raises an ERC-20 allowance, often to unlimited, for a chosen spender

0xa22cb465.name: setApprovalForAll(address,bool)
0xa22cb465.risk: Grants operator rights over ALL of a wallet's NFTs in a collection

0xa9059cbb.name: transfer(address,uint256)
0xa9059cbb.risk: Direct token transfer — dangerous only if the destination is attacker-controlled

0xd505accf.name: permit(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint8,bytes32,bytes32)
0xd505accf.risk: Off-chain EIP-2612 approval — gasless, no on-chain record until the attacker submits it

meta.name: Tinfoil Scan — wallet drainer signature list
meta.policy: Only signatures verified from real published sources go in as 'verified'. Anything inferred goes in as 'heuristic' and is weighted lower. Static domain blocklists are intentionally NOT included — modern kits (Inferno et al.) deploy single-use contracts and rotate phishing domains faster than any list can track, so code fingerprints + behavioral patterns carry the detection weight.

obfuscation_indicators.detail: eval() usage in page scripts. Classic obfuscation vehicle.
obfuscator.io-style variable names (_0x...). Heavy obfuscation on a mint page is a red flag.
Nested atob() decoding — layered payload decoding.
document.write(unescape(...)) — vintage but still used to hide drainer payloads.
Very long base64 blob embedded in JS. Could be a bundled asset — or an encoded payload.

page_trait_patterns.detail: Hidden iframe — used to load attacker infrastructure or exfiltrate without visible UI.
Clipboard hijacking — drainers swap copied addresses so pasted sends go to the attacker.
Page prompts wallet connection. Normal for web3 — the danger is what it asks you to SIGN next.

rules: score = min(100, sum of finding weights)
any single critical finding forces at least SUSPICIOUS
two or more critical findings force DANGEROUS
info findings never move the score

script_filename_heuristics.detail: Suspicious only as a renamed lookalike; legit web3modal is a real library. Flagged for manual review.

signature_request_patterns.detail: EIP-712 typed-data signature request. The delivery vehicle for Permit and Permit2 phishing — gasless and invisible until the attacker submits it.
EIP-712 typed-data signature request (older variant). Same permit-phishing risk as v4.
Generic EIP-712 signature request. Legit dapps use it (login, orders) — context decides.
Raw eth_sign of arbitrary data — the most dangerous signature type. Most wallets cannot decode what is being signed. (Note: eth_signTypedData variants are matched by their own patterns.)
personal_sign request. Usually benign (login), but drainers have used it for hex-encoded payloads — check the message content.
Uniswap Permit2 typed data. One phished Permit2 signature can reach every token the victim ever approved to Permit2.
EIP-2612 Permit type definition in EIP-712 types. Needed by legit gasless flows too — weight rises when paired with unknown spender addresses.
EIP-7702 delegation pattern. Malicious EIP-7702 signatures (emerged post-Pectra, 2025) temporarily convert an EOA into a smart contract the attacker controls.
